items.title: $p$-elementary and $p$-hyperelementary finite groups
Subgroups of $p$-elementary and $p$-hyperelementary groups retain the type
items.strategy: For a subgroup of $C\times P$, take its $p'$-part and its Sylow $p$-subgroup to recover the direct product. For a subgroup of $C\rtimes P$, intersect with the normal cyclic $p'$-subgroup and use a Sylow $p$-subgroup; the order calculation gives the required semidirect product. Treat $C=1$, $P=1$, and the trivial subgroup in the same argument.

items.title: The induction ideal attached to a family of subgroups
An induction ideal is an ideal in the character ring
items.strategy: Write an element as a finite sum of induction images and apply the already-published projection formula to every summand. This is the general-family form needed here; the earlier cyclic-family lemma is deliberately not silently reused outside its stated scope.

items.title: The $p$-primary congruence for integral character values
items.strategy: For an integral-valued element of the cyclotomic coefficient character ring, restrict to the cyclic subgroup generated by $g$, expand in its linear characters, and compare $g$ with its $p'$-part using the Frobenius congruence in the cyclotomic integer ring. The conclusion is made only under the integral-value hypothesis used by Kramár.

items.title: The hyperelementary permutation subring reduces the unit problem to elementary subgroups
items.strategy: Use Mackey decomposition and subgroup closure to show that the integer span of permutation characters induced from hyperelementary subgroups is a subring. Then make the reduction explicit: a unit relation in that subring, together with the induction-on-order reduction for each hyperelementary subgroup, transports by transitivity into the elementary induction ideal. No unproved hyperelementary permutation relation is assumed.

items.title: Banaschewski's prime obstruction for a proper ring of integer-valued functions
items.strategy: For each point $x$ take the additive subgroup of values as $n_x\mathbb Z$. If every $n_x=1$, choose one function with value $1$ at each point and multiply the finitely many complements to manufacture the unit; the contrapositive supplies $x$ and a prime divisor of $n_x$. Apply this only to the hyperelementary permutation subring, whose values are integral.

items.title: A $p$-elementary induction image detects a fixed element modulo $p$
items.strategy: Record both sourced local forms at a fixed prime and element. Li's form constructs from the normalizer of the $p'$-part a $p$-hyperelementary subgroup whose induced trivial permutation character is nonzero modulo $p$; this is the detector that negates the Banaschewski obstruction. Kramár's form takes a Sylow $p$-subgroup of the relevant centralizer and induces delta class functions from $p$-elementary subgroups; the $p$-primary congruence transfers its nonzero value from the $p'$-part to the original element. Its cyclotomic-coefficient and integral-value qualifications are retained.

items.title: Isaacs's fixed-point criterion for a linear character in the hyperelementary reduction
items.strategy: Let the Sylow $p$-subgroup act on a fibre of a linear character of the normal $p'$-part. Orbit counting makes the fibre meet the fixed-point subgroup; the stated kernel hypothesis then forces its value to be $1$. This supplies the proper-stabilizer step in the induction-on-order reduction and is not conflated with the later global monomial-character theory.

items.title: Supersolvable finite groups and monomial characters
$p$-elementary finite groups are supersolvable
items.strategy: Build a normal cyclic-factor series for the cyclic $p'$-factor. For the finite $p$-factor, induct on order: a central subgroup of order $p$ exists, its quotient is again a $p$-group, and lifting the quotient series gives a normal cyclic-factor series. Combine the two direct-product series. This proves precisely the structural input used by the monomiality argument.

items.title: A faithful irreducible character with a noncentral normal abelian subgroup comes from a proper inertia subgroup
items.strategy: Restrict the representation to the normal abelian subgroup and decompose it into its linear-character weight spaces. The group permutes the weights transitively by irreducibility. Noncentrality makes a weight stabilizer proper, and the direct sum of its conjugate weight spaces identifies the representation with induction from the stabilizer. This is tom Dieck's Proposition 4.3.2 written as the focused proper-induction step.

items.title: A nonabelian supersolvable group has a noncentral normal abelian subgroup
items.strategy: Choose the first noncentral term in a normal series with cyclic factors. Its predecessor is central, while its commutators with the whole group lie in that predecessor; the commutator calculation makes the chosen term abelian and preserves normality. This is the exact structural branch needed by the faithful case of the monomiality induction.

items.title: Monomiality lifts along a quotient
items.strategy: For a representation whose kernel contains a normal subgroup $N$, factor it through $G/N$. Pull back the inducing subgroup and its linear character from the quotient, identify the inflated induced representation with the corresponding induction upstairs, and use induction transitivity. This isolates the nonfaithful branch of the supersolvable induction.

items.title: Every finite supersolvable group is monomial
items.strategy: Induct on group order and apply the three focused reductions. A nonfaithful irreducible descends and lifts by the quotient lemma. A faithful irreducible of an abelian group is linear; otherwise the normal-abelian lemma and proper-inertia proposition reduce it to a proper supersolvable subgroup, whose inducing character is monomial by induction. Induction transitivity completes the proof.

items.title: Characters of $p$-elementary groups are induced from linear characters
items.strategy: Apply the local supersolvability lemma to $C\times P$, then apply the immediately preceding monomiality theorem to each irreducible constituent. Add the resulting integral expressions. This gives the exact linear-character conversion required in Brauer induction without importing the later monomial-character page.

items.title: Brauer induction from linear characters of elementary subgroups
items.strategy: Let the elementary induction ideal be generated by all $p$-elementary subgroups. The general ideal lemma reduces the theorem to placing $1_G$ in it. Follow Li's proved route: the hyperelementary permutation span is a subring; a Banaschewski obstruction would give a prime and element; the fixed-element construction contradicts that obstruction; the Isaacs induction-on-order step converts the resulting hyperelementary relation to elementary induction. Finally apply the preceding linearization lemma inside each elementary subgroup and induction transitivity. Kramár's local congruence construction is retained as an independent check on the $p$-local part of this route.

items.title: Restriction to elementary subgroups detects generalized characters
items.strategy: Use the unit relation furnished by Brauer induction and multiply it by a generalized character. The projection formula rewrites every term as an induction of the corresponding elementary restriction, so simultaneous zero restrictions force the original character to vanish.

items.title: Elementary restrictions characterize generalized characters over a splitting field
items.strategy: State the source's precise splitting-field version. The forward direction is restriction-stability; for the reverse direction multiply the Brauer unit relation by the class function and use the projection formula, so the assumed generalized-character restrictions yield a generalized character of $G$.

items.title: A cyclotomic field containing the needed roots of unity splits a finite group
items.strategy: Let $m$ be an exponent of $G$. Brauer induction expresses an irreducible complex representation as an integral combination of inductions of linear characters from elementary subgroups. Their values are $m$-th roots of unity, hence lie in a characteristic-zero field containing them; semisimplicity and independence of irreducible classes then descend the representation itself. Record $\mathbb Q(\zeta_{|G|})$ as the immediate, not necessarily minimal, choice.

title: Brauer Induction and Elementary Subgroups — Examples

items.title: Elementary and hyperelementary structures in small groups
items.strategy: For distinct primes, exhibit $C_{pq}$ as a direct product of its $p'$ and $p$ factors. Contrast it with $S_3$ and $D_{2p}$ as nontrivial semidirect products, and include a concrete $C_7\rtimes C_3$ example. Check explicitly which examples are elementary and which are only hyperelementary.

items.title: Integral Brauer-induction expressions for the irreducible characters of $S_3$
items.strategy: Calculate induction from $C_2$ and $A_3=C_3$: the nontrivial linear character of $C_3$ induces the degree-two irreducible, while the two permutation characters give the trivial and sign constituents. Solve these integral identities for all three irreducibles, keeping every inducing subgroup elementary.

items.title: Trivial factors in the definition of an elementary group
items.strategy: Verify directly that $C=1$ gives a $p$-group, $P=1$ gives a cyclic $p'$-group, and $C=P=1$ gives the trivial group. Explain why all three satisfy the same order and direct-product conventions as the nondegenerate cases.

items.title: Cyclic subgroups do not suffice for integral induction in $A_5$
items.strategy: Every cyclic subgroup of $A_5$ has order $1$, $2$, $3$, or $5$, hence every character induced from a linear character of one has even degree. An integral linear combination of them still has even degree, whereas $1_{A_5}$ has degree one. This proves nonmembership without relying merely on a particular rational Artin formula.
